scope: Read-only causal diagnosis of the two-page assessment native test conflict expectation. Actual React hook and actual DraftStore transaction code; fake-indexeddb supplies an in-process IndexedDB implementation. Separate journal factories model independent page-memory owners. No real HTTP/native browser in this probe.

original_native_failure.test: two pages preserve independent local CAS candidates; a later submitted snapshot never accepts restored edits
original_native_failure.failure: Expected local-conflict heading count 0 while page B remained open with dirty candidate B.

controlled_probe.test: live dirty owner B republishes its removed candidate; closing durable B first allows single-owner resolution
steps: Mount A with its own page-memory journal and DraftStore; save dirty candidate A and await durability.
Mount B with a different page-memory journal and DraftStore connected to the same IDB database; save dirty candidate B and await durability.
Observe A display both candidate texts.
A explicitly resolves to its displayed candidate while B remains mounted.
Observe A transaction has removed B; then B journal invokes the actual store.save with expectedRevision=0 and the preserved candidate B reappears.
Await both queues settled and B unsafe=false; unmount and close B.
A resolves again as the only active writer.

later_output_capture_attempt.note: Same unchanged probe rerun solely to request console trace; runner emitted summary only. Assertions in retained source verify the causal sequence; no extra trace output claimed.

conclusion: The revived B candidate is intentional preservation by a still-active dirty owner, not evidence that A failed to commit its explicit resolution. The native expectation of persistent zero conflicts while B still owns B is invalid.
recommended_native_sequence: After both candidates are visibly durable, explicitly close the safe B page, then choose A with one active writer and assert the resolved state. Keep the later terminal-snapshot protections intact. Do not weaken remember/enqueue preservation.

production_cause.behavior: A missing stored dirty branch is remembered in page memory; once pending is zero, its absent candidate is enqueued using fixed expectedRevision=0 to preserve it as a conflict.

limitations: Uses a minimal synthetic journal envelope decoder to isolate ownership/CAS; strict assessment envelope validation is outside this probe.
Does not independently rerun the seven native cases or imply their eventual all-pass result.
changes: No repository source, test, Git or progress modifications. Original native failure and all temporary probe inputs/output retained.
